lesson.title: El Salto de Números: A Number Hop Game
lesson.subject: spanish

contentBlocks.text: Sol set up five dots on the floor today, numbered uno through cinco. Get your jumping feet ready!
Look down at the floor dots. When Sol calls a number, jump to that dot! If Sol says '¡Dos!', jump to the dot for dos.
Sol will call the numbers in a mixed-up order now — listen carefully before you jump! Try uno, cinco, tres, cuatro, and dos in any order.
You listened for each number and jumped to the right dot every time — fantastic listening! Tomorrow is our counting show for Sol.

objectives: Jump to the correct floor spot (1-5) after hearing a spoken Spanish number
Recognize all five numbers uno-cinco out of the counting-song order
materialsNeeded: Five pieces of paper or tape marks on the floor, numbered/dotted 1 through 5
Open floor space to jump safely
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Lay out five spots on the floor in a row or scattered, one for each number 1-5 (draw dots, write numerals, or just use paper squares).
2. Stand near Sol and call out a number in Spanish, e.g. '¡Tres!' — model jumping to that spot yourself first.
3. Have your child listen and jump to the matching spot each time you or Sol calls a number.
4. Call the numbers in mixed-up order (not always 1-2-3-4-5) so your child is truly listening, not just following a pattern.
5. Swap roles: let your child call a number for you (or Sol) to jump to.
6. Complete the on-screen speed-drill activity together, cheering each correct match.
7. Close by asking: 'Which number was the trickiest to listen for today?'
differentiationTips: Struggling: call the numbers in order (uno, dos, tres...) for the first few rounds before mixing them up
Ready for more: call two numbers in a row and have your child jump to both spots in sequence
A near-miss jump to the neighboring dot is a great sign your child is listening closely — celebrate the attempt
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a spoken listening-and-jumping activity — success looks like your child jumping toward the correct spot after hearing a number, not a written answer. In the speed-drill game, each English number word matches its Spanish counterpart: one → uno, two → dos, three → tres, four → cuatro, five → cinco.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Deepens week 3's WA-WL-2015.1.2 target by requiring the child to recognize each number out of the predictable 1-2-3-4-5 song order — true listening comprehension rather than memorized sequence — and the on-screen speed drill gives the same recognition skill a fast-paced digital rep.
